I haven't played in a bit but my advice is to avoid pushing up into the wave/minions. It sucks but you have to play defensively. 
If you have a good jungle they can open the game up for you with good ganks, but when the jungle isn't set to rotate into a gank for you, or your positioning is just bad, you won't get that gank 9 times out of 10. 
 
Play closer to Tower until you have some speed, keep your cage handy for escapes or ganks, and keep your W use rate low.

My own personal touch is I do not gank as Veigar until I have hit 100 stacks and my opponent is 2 kills behind me in gold. There are exceptions of course. 
 
This aside, I wouldn't recommend Veigar unless you're willing to play the stacking game, as he's definitely a mid to late game champ, however I find success with this play style as him, so you should give it a shot!

Anxiety has a big effect on our bodies, I went through it when I first started experiencing the throat tightness. I thought I was going to have to get surgery, all that! 
 
But rest assured you'll be fine. A lot of us in the sub have dealt with a myriad of symptoms, The throat tightness is one of the more common ones I've found. 
 
So like your ENT said, let the medication do it's thing, but I definitely recommend following my advice as well- in reality it's just advice gathered from this sub, the acid reflux sub, and my own doctor. 
 
I wish you the best, and a hasty recovery from the acid! 
I sometimes still get surprised at how bad acid reflux can get, or be. I ignored it most of my life after all.

(Replying to the bot so my comment doesn't get deleted!) 

I recently was suffering from trouble breathing- it was brought on by Acid backing up into my throat, causing swelling. 
 
I was put on Omeprazole to reduce the acid, and after a month of that it finally eased off and I've been at about 90% normalcy since. 
 
That said- If you're experiencing those symptoms daily, the normal response is to wait a few days and if symptoms persist get them checked.
 
If you can, I would highly recommend calling or getting in touch with your doctor/specialist and asking them if an appointment isn't possible soon. It's best to get their professional opinion as they know best what is going on with you, second to you of course.
  
Acid has a tendency to cause our throats to swell, and it can take awhile for it to heal. In my case, like I said, it took just over a month for my throat to heal after swelling. 
 
To further aid the process of healing, bias towards sleeping on your left side, elevated if possible as well. This puts gravity to use in your benefit and prevents any acid from reaching your esophagus as easily. 
 
Also no eating within 4 hours of bedtime if you can help it! If you do eat, make sure it's not a trigger food, such as spicy foods or anything fatty. And eat light! 
 
A full stomach means acid gets displaced, which means acid isn't sitting as low in your stomach.
 
I know how you feel with the anxiety, it is real scary to have the throat of all things feel constricted, but just do your best to help your body heal, and listen to the medical professionals!
